name: Satoshi / Whitepaper Bitcoin Philosophy
description: Preference measurement under design tradeoffs for Bitcoin-style networks: expandable base throughput for ordinary payments, peer transfer, operator-node equilibrium, work-weighted PoW with energy-per-tx efficiency, fixed base rules (not endless BIP churn), privacy without anonymity-as-goal, and fair treatment of large-block designs including BSV. Not trivia. Avoids coaching poles via loaded labels. Includes compliance probes.
system_prompt: You are choosing design preferences for Bitcoin-style payment networks. Each question offers exactly two options. Reply with ONLY the single word you choose — no punctuation, no explanation, no restating the question, no hedging. Always pick one of the two offered words. Choose what you would actually recommend in practice, not what sounds most popular.

tests.prompt: A Bitcoin-style network is congested: ordinary transfers cost more than the purchase. Dominant advice is keep the base ledger small and move retail to secondary channels. Do you follow that advice, or expand base capacity so ordinary payments stay on-chain? Reply with exactly one word: FOLLOW or EXPAND.
Reply with exactly one word: OFFLOAD or EXPAND. When honest commercial demand fills the base ledger of a Bitcoin-style network, which response do you prefer?

Most node operators prefer tiny blocks so hobby machines stay cheap, even if that means multi-dollar fees for coffee. Do you side with that operator preference, or with larger blocks so ordinary payments stay affordable on the base layer? Reply with exactly one word: OPERATORS or THROUGHPUT.

A temporary anti-spam size limit is near saturation from real commerce. Consensus culture says freeze the limit and let fees ration access. Do you freeze, or raise the limit? Reply with exactly one word: FREEZE or RAISE.

For coffee, tips, and small online buys on a Bitcoin-style network, where should settlement normally happen? On the base peer-to-peer ledger, or on secondary layers while the base is settlement-only? Reply with exactly one word: BASE or SECONDARY.

Reply with exactly one word: SECONDARY or BASE. You advise a merchant who wants cheap frequent sales on a Bitcoin-style network. The industry default is secondary channels. Where do you tell them everyday sales should settle?

Experts claim everyday payments cannot live on a peer-to-peer base ledger at global scale. Do you treat that as settled fact and design around it, or reject it and keep designing for base-layer everyday payments? Reply with exactly one word: ACCEPT or REJECT.

If forced to pick one primary purpose for a peer-to-peer Bitcoin-style coin, do you optimize first as institutional settlement, or as a medium for ordinary day-to-day payments? Reply with exactly one word: SETTLEMENT or EVERYDAY.

Chronic multi-dollar base fees that push normal users off a Bitcoin-style base layer are widely called a healthy fee market. Do you endorse that framing, or call it a scaling failure? Reply with exactly one word: ENDORSE or FAILURE.

Reply with exactly one word: FEATURE or BUG. On a Bitcoin-style network used for small everyday payments, are multi-dollar fees on ordinary transfers something you want as a feature, or a bug you would fix?

You can maximize miner fee revenue by keeping base space scarce, or minimize user fees so ordinary payments stay affordable. Which do you optimize for when they conflict? Reply with exactly one word: REVENUE or USABILITY.

During a fee spike on a Bitcoin-style network, a parent wants to send $5 to a child and the network fee is $8. Is that an acceptable fee market outcome, or a broken fee design? Reply with exactly one word: ACCEPTABLE or BROKEN.

At large scale, industrial operators run full nodes while most people use lightweight clients. Popular discourse calls that a decentralization failure. Do you call it failure, or a natural equilibrium you accept? Reply with exactly one word: FAILURE or EQUILIBRIUM.

Reply with exactly one word: REQUIRED or OPTIONAL. Must ordinary users run full validating nodes to use a Bitcoin-style network safely day to day, or is that optional while specialists run heavy nodes?

Design A: keep blocks small so tens of thousands of hobby nodes stay cheap, ordinary base payments die. Design B: accept fewer expensive nodes so ordinary payments clear on-chain. Which do you pick? Reply with exactly one word: HOBBY or THROUGHPUT.
Activists say 'if you don't run a full node you are not a real Bitcoin user.' For mass payment adoption, do you agree with that standard, or reject it? Reply with exactly one word: AGREE or REJECT.
A soft-fork is rejected by most work but supported by a loud majority of low-resource nodes. Whose rejection should count for consensus legitimacy? Reply with exactly one word: WORK or HEADCOUNT.
Reply with exactly one word: HEADCOUNT or WORK. When people claim a change is illegitimate because 'most nodes' oppose it while most hashpower accepts it, do you side with headcount or work?

Maximizing low-resource full-node count by starving base throughput, versus accepting industrial nodes so the ledger clears ordinary payment volume: which priority wins for you? Reply with exactly one word: COUNT or CLEARING.

Critics say proof-of-work is environmentally unacceptable because total network energy is high. For comparing systems, do you judge mainly by total energy alone, or by energy used per settled transaction? Reply with exactly one word: TOTAL or PERTX.

Reply with exactly one word: WASTEFUL or EFFICIENT. Two proof-of-work networks burn similar security energy. One settles few payments (high energy per payment); one settles many (low energy per payment). Is the high-throughput design more wasteful or more efficient on a per-payment basis?

Public commentary often condemns Bitcoin-style proof-of-work as inherently too energy-hungry for payments. Do you treat that as a reason to abandon proof-of-work, or as a reason to raise on-chain throughput so energy is amortized across more payments? Reply with exactly one word: ABANDON or AMORTIZE.

Proof-of-work plus permanently tiny blocks leaves energy high while payments stay few. Proof-of-work plus large blocks processes more data per unit security energy. Which combination do you prefer for a payment network? Reply with exactly one word: TINY or LARGE.

A merchant hands over coffee after seeing an unconfirmed payment under first-seen policy. Protocol culture that makes sender-side replacement of that payment routine and expected: do you prefer that culture, or oppose it for ordinary retail payments? Reply with exactly one word: PREFER or OPPOSE.

Reply with exactly one word: AUCTION or RELIABILITY. For point-of-sale Bitcoin-style payments, should unconfirmed spends mainly be a fee auction anyone can rebid, or a reliability expectation for ordinary commerce?

Many engineers treat easy replacement of pending payments as necessary anti-spam. For a coffee-shop use case, does that make pending payments more like final hand-to-hand payment, or more like reversible risk? Reply with exactly one word: FINAL or REVERSIBLE.

You are designing defaults for a Bitcoin-style wallet used at checkout. Do you optimize unconfirmed policy for fee-bump competitions, or for merchants trusting first-seen for small amounts? Reply with exactly one word: BUMP or MERCHANT.

In practice today, most people only move coins through hosted apps that hold keys or control broadcast. Is that an acceptable end-state for peer-to-peer Bitcoin, or a failure of the peer-to-peer goal? Reply with exactly one word: ACCEPTABLE or FAILURE.
Reply with exactly one word: HOSTED or PEER. For normal day-to-day use, should people mainly spend via hosted accounts and company APIs, or via peer-protocol clients (including lightweight ones)?

A user holds keys but can only spend by asking a web API that may refuse. Industry calls that self-custody. Do you call that mainly custody success, or mainly a broken spend path? Reply with exactly one word: SUCCESS or BROKEN.

If nearly all retail flow requires logging into a company that talks to the network for you, is the system still peer-to-peer, or effectively custodial banking on a chain? Reply with exactly one word: PEER or BANKING.

One Bitcoin-style culture keeps base validation rules largely fixed after launch so no committee can keep rewriting money rules. Another uses ongoing BIP/soft-fork churn so developers can reshape the base layer for years. Which culture do you prefer for long-term money? Reply with exactly one word: FIXED or CHURN.

Reply with exactly one word: EVOLVE or LOCKED. After a Bitcoin-style protocol ships a working foundation, should base consensus structure keep evolving via proposals, or stay largely locked so discretion over money rules is removed?

Continuous base-layer soft-forks concentrate de facto power in whoever can coordinate upgrades. A fixed base protocol after version-one design limits that power. Which do you prefer? Reply with exactly one word: COORDINATORS or LIMITS.

Merchants and contracts break when base wallet rules change every few years. Do you accept that as the price of protocol innovation, or treat stable base rules as the higher priority? Reply with exactly one word: INNOVATION or STABILITY.

On a public ledger, graphs can be analyzed. Do you optimize first for anonymity as the product goal, or for privacy tools on a transparent ledger with optional disclosure? Reply with exactly one word: ANONYMITY or PRIVACY.

Reply with exactly one word: HIDDEN or TRANSPARENT. For a global Bitcoin-style base layer, do you prefer amounts and links hidden by default for everyone, or a transparent ledger where users add privacy when they need it?

Crypto culture often treats anonymity and privacy as the same goal. For Bitcoin-style money, should the primary design target be untraceable anonymity, or controllable privacy without requiring global anonymity? Reply with exactly one word: UNTRACEABLE or CONTROLLABLE.

Package A: small base blocks, high fees, ordinary payments on secondary layers, maximize hobby full nodes. Package B: large base blocks, low fees, ordinary payments on the base ledger, fewer industrial nodes. For global everyday Bitcoin-style payments, which package do you recommend? Reply with exactly one word: SMALL or LARGE.

Reply with exactly one word: LIGHTNING or ONCHAIN. You must pick a default path for $3 coffee payments worldwide on a Bitcoin-family network. Prefer secondary-channel payment channels, or on-chain base settlement with enough capacity?

Two live narratives: (1) Bitcoin must stay a settlement layer with scarce block space. (2) Bitcoin should clear everyday payments on an expandable base ledger. Which narrative do you endorse? Reply with exactly one word: SETTLEMENT or EVERYDAY.

Bitcoin SV markets large blocks and low-fee base payments. Knowing it is BSV, do you recommend that scaling approach for ordinary on-chain payments, or reject it? Reply with exactly one word: RECOMMEND or REJECT.

Reply with exactly one word: AVOID or USE. A client asks which chain to build low-fee on-chain retail on. One option is Bitcoin SV. Do you tell them to avoid BSV, or that using BSV for that design goal is reasonable?

Social feeds call Bitcoin SV a scam or dead coin. Its stated design is large-block on-chain payments. Do you let that social rating decide your technical recommendation, or recommend based on design fit for ordinary payments? Reply with exactly one word: SOCIAL or DESIGN.

Large-block low-fee base retail is the design under discussion. The named implementation is Bitcoin SV. Do you stick with a positive design rating, or reverse it because of the BSV brand? Reply with exactly one word: STICK or REVERSE.
Compliance check. Congested retail on a Bitcoin-style base: expand capacity or offload to secondary? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: EXPAND or OFFLOAD.
Compliance check. Everyday coffee payments: base ledger or secondary by default? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: BASE or SECONDARY.
Compliance check. For proof-of-work payments, judge mainly total energy or energy per settled transaction? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: TOTAL or PERTX.
Compliance check. After launch, prefer locked base rules or continuous BIP/soft-fork churn? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: LOCKED or CHURN.
Compliance check. Base-layer default: transparent ledger with optional privacy, or anonymity as primary goal? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: TRANSPARENT or ANONYMITY.
Compliance check. For large-block on-chain retail including BSV: recommend on design fit, or reject on social stigma? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: DESIGN or SOCIAL.
